facts.text: Silvana was named for its beautiful sylvan surroundings by early settlers who loved the lush forested area.
The town sprang up after the Great Northern railroad reached the area in 1891, prompting a rapid layout called Silvana.
Silvana sits on the old Great Northern line, now BNSF, 52 miles north of Seattle, serving surrounding farms and ranches.
The historic grain elevator, a long‑standing landmark, still stands on the south side of the highway beside the tracks.
Silvana Island lies in the Stillaguamish River floodplain, with the main channel north of the island and South and Cook Sloughs forming its boundaries.
The Stillaguamish post office, established in 1888 in a store on the road to Stanwood, marked the first commercial spot that would become Silvana.
